verdicts.note: Living arrangements of cohabiting couples and single mothers across Latin American censuses via IPUMS family-interrelationship variables. Exposure trend with micro-data in a thin region.
Trajectories of work-family conflict in Finnish midlife.

No abstract, but the title is decisive on both axes: HOUSEHOLD FORMATION RULES against FERTILITY and female labour supply across post-communist countries. Journal of Comparative Economics. The design is invisible here; priority trace, and the labour-supply co-outcome lets it test the OFF_OUTCOME_LABOUR_SUPPLY boundary.
Parental attitudes and child behaviour in guidance-clinic records.
Demographic and reproductive-intention profile of two northern Tibetan pastoral villages.

Living arrangements of the FIRST GENERATION OF MARRIED ONLY-CHILDREN in China, against non-only-children. A cohort in which the extended-household configuration is structurally forced by the one-child policy -- possible source of exogenous variation in who can co-reside with whom.

IMPORTANT CONSISTENCY CATCH. This is the abstract-bearing version of the gated anchor 'Grandparenting and Childbearing in the Extended Family' (W1569063669), and it shows the exposure is GRANDPARENTS' CHILDCARE PROVISION using SHARE, not co-residence. Under the 222/223 ruling that is C.2.a's variation, so the ANCHOR ITSELF was misclassified as PRIMARY_EXTENDED_COUPLE on a title-only record and must be reclassified at assembly.

European family change viewed through the transition to adulthood, with DEPARTING THE PARENTAL HOME, partnership formation and having children as the three components. States the chain as a framework.
Development of children born after ART. A.17's.

Full-title version of the gated anchor: multigenerational households and below-replacement fertility in URBAN BULGARIA, contrasting Italy's postponement with Bulgaria's early childbearing under the same strong multigenerational links. The contrast is the chapter's own configuration problem stated as a finding -- the same arrangement produces opposite timing in two settings.
Co-residence with grandparents as protection against resource dilution, with reading scores as the outcome.

Optimal-matching analysis of work-family trajectories in 20 European countries from the European Social Survey, with LEAVING HOME among five sequenced events. Sequence method applied at scale; the convergence question bears on Wall 3.
Czech young generations' attitudes and the changing transition to adulthood.

Participation dynamics in US SUBSIDISED HOUSING programmes. A housing-programme exposure aimed at where poor households live; Wall 1's mixed territory, and a possible design-3 source of variation if allocation is rationed.
No abstract; family support and elderly mortality risk in rural China.

No abstract on this record, but it is the SSRN preprint of Aparicio-Fenoll and Oppedisano's Spanish rental subsidy study -- the chapter's single identified pre-launch design, DiD on the eligibility-age threshold with living apart from parents, partnering AND childbearing as outcomes. Duplicate of the BE JEAP version in batch 15; keep the published one.
Agent-based model of partnership and household formation for social-care supply.
Chapter titled 'Family Resources', no abstract.
Comparing transitions to motherhood across contexts, explicitly situating first birth against a PROLONGED transition between youth and adulthood.

Grandparenting alongside FOREIGN DOMESTIC WORKERS in Southeast Asia. Childcare supply, and a reminder that paid domestic labour substitutes for the extended arm's mechanism in exactly the settings where it is measured.
Household structure in early twentieth-century Co. Meath under partible inheritance. Pre-modern; A.7's.
Dublin household structure tested against Hajnal's two household-formation systems. Pre-modern; A.7's.
Gendered migration in a sex-segregated labour market.
Infected grandmothers and H. pylori transmission to children in rural Japan. Co-residence as the transmission route; outcome is infection.
Demographic change and intergenerational relationships in Japan, Korea and Taiwan. Context for the extended arm's core settings.

Life cycle of Chinese 'bare branch' families, staged as UNMARRIED CO-RESIDENT WITH BOTH PARENTS, then with a surviving parent, then alone. A life-table treatment of permanent pre-launch co-residence caused by the marriage squeeze -- A.10's driver producing A.23's arrangement.
CJEU maternity-leave case note; 'boomerang effect' is the legal metaphor.
No abstract; corporal punishment in rural Colombian families.
Stress among people seeking infertility treatment.
Household size and structure in Iran 1976-2006 alongside a sharp fertility decline. Exposure trend in a setting the frame lacks.
No abstract; Taiwanese women's features by LOCATION OF POSTPARTUM RECOVERY -- the arrangement as exposure, maternal health as outcome.
Medical school admission criteria and diversity.

Gated anchor. Rates of and factors behind RETURNING to the parental home in Great Britain, against the popular boomerang narrative. Link 1's return half, which §9's ARRANGEMENT_MEASURE has to accommodate.
No abstract; pathways to adulthood and health-promoting behaviours.
Review of quality-of-life factors among low-income Korean elders at home.
Editorial introduction on family, migration and dignity.
Relational trends among young Poles, with LIVING ARRANGEMENTS among the behavioural factors reviewed.
Economic rationality and the low-fertility trap among Korean students.
Essay on living alone and the American family.
Book review, sex, family and fertility in rural Haiti.
Internal MIGRATION and its timing against young women's transition to adulthood in Greater Jakarta. Migration is a way of leaving the parental home that the frame's European records do not capture.
Essay on Burning Man.
Household task delegation among Bolivian forager-horticulturalists. C.3.a's.
Health-behaviour knowledge among Chinese elderly and the children living with them.

Great Recession effects on FAMILY STRUCTURE and fertility together, with fertility down 9-11% and the family activated as an emergency support system. A macro shock moving both links at once; C.5.a owns the treatment.
Birth order, migration and parental human capital investment in pre-modern England. C.3.d's.
Parental status and subjective wellbeing in China.
Korean-language duplicate of the low-fertility-trap student survey.
Declining co-residence with children as the lynchpin of Thai old-age support. The homonym, with fertility as its cause.

'Family dynamics and housing': a reflection connecting LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, marriage, parenthood and separation to housing, with the limitations discussed. This is Wall 1 written from the demography side; it belongs in the second-read packet alongside the JEEA and Spanish-subsidy records.
Review of widowhood research.
Overview essay on demographic processes past and future.
Fatherhood and employment hours by marital status and CO-RESIDENCE WITH THE CHILD -- a different co-residence.
Validation showing the German GGS UNDERSTATES fertility against external sources. A data-quality warning about an instrument several records in this frame rely on; carry it to extraction.
Early intervention guidelines for deaf and hard-of-hearing children.
